Combine multi-drug predictions into a single combination score

Source: R/predict.R
combine_drugs.Rd

Implements the IDA (Independent Drug Action) combination principle used in PERCEPTION: each clone-level drug viability is first z-score scaled across all clones, then the per-clone combined score is derived from the drug-specific z-scores. The default rule min means "the most effective drug in the combination drives the clone-level combined score" — the exact rule hard-coded in the Shiny app's internal combo_clone_frame().

Usage

combine_drugs(
  pred,
  patient = NULL,
  clone_id = NULL,
  combine_rule = c("min", "mean", "max", "median"),
  na.rm = TRUE,
  include_single_z = FALSE
)

Arguments

pred

Matrix or data.frame of clone-level drug viability predictions. Typically the output of predict_drugs(). Rows = clones, columns = drugs. Row names must be canonical PERCEPTION clone keys ("patient@clone_id"). Alternatively, pass a data.frame with an explicit patient column and a clone_id column.

patient

Optional character vector of patient IDs, length equal to nrow(pred). Required only when pred row names are NOT "patient@clone_id" keys.

clone_id

Optional character vector of clone IDs, length equal to nrow(pred). Required only when passing patient explicitly.

combine_rule

Character scalar, per-clone aggregation after z-scoring. Must be one of "min" (IDA default), "mean", "max", or "median".

na.rm

Logical, passed through to the aggregator. Default TRUE.

include_single_z

Logical. If TRUE, per-drug z-scored columns are retained in the output alongside comb_viability. Default FALSE.

Value

A data.frame with columns:

patient

Patient ID.

clone_id

Clone ID.

comb_viability

Combined viability score (already z-scored across clones, so predict_patients() will not standardise it again).

<drug_z>

(optional, when include_single_z = TRUE) one additional column per input drug, named like <drug>.z, containing the per-drug z-scores before combination.

Details

This function is the missing glue between predict_drugs() and downstream patient-level aggregation / visualisation. Its output feeds directly into predict_patients() (as the app's predict_patients() already skips re-standardising the comb_viability column) and plot_clone_viability().

Pipeline


  pred     <- predict_drugs(models, rank_expr)        # clones x drugs matrix
  clone_df <- combine_drugs(pred)                    # patient / clone_id / comb_viability
  pat      <- predict_patients(clone_df, prepared_data)
  plot_clone_viability(clone_df, viability_var = "comb_viability")

The patient-level aggregated score will be identical to the one produced by the Shiny app for the same drugs / clones.

Caveats

The default min rule amplifies noise when individual drug models are very poor — the "least bad" model can still be quite bad, but min picks it as the best combination driver. For exploratory analyses you can pass combine_rule = "mean" or combine_rule = "max" and compare.

When only one drug is present in pred, the combined score is simply that drug's z-score.

See also

predict_drugs(), predict_patients(), plot_clone_viability(), zscore_viability()
